title: Completeness of integer multiplicity currents: a mass-summable series of IM currents has an IM sum (Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13)
statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K. X_j ⇀ Y (WeaklyConvergesOn) means X_j(ω) → Y(ω) for every ω. V ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained V U) means that closure V is compact and contained in U. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and let X_r ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) be IM with Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞ (sum in [0, ∞]). Then there is an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) converges to Y(ω) (HasSum), and M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). This is Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 (completeness of the IM currents with respect to the mass semi-norms), applied to the partial sums of the series.
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → (∀ r, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X r)) → ∑' r, (X r).mass ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), HasSum (fun r => X r ω) (Y ω)) ∧ Y.mass ≤ ∑' r, (X r).mass
